settings.language.label: Language & region
settings.language.description: Sets the interface language, and how dates and numbers are formatted.
settings.language.hint:
Chooses the language the interface is shown in **and** how dates, times and numbers are formatted — e.g. `31/12/2026` vs `12/31/2026`, and the thousands/decimal separators.

A language without a full translation shows any untranslated text in English. This does not change your currency.
settings.pagination.paginate.label: Paginate long lists
settings.pagination.paginate.description: Split long lists into numbered pages with a page control, instead of one continuously-scrolling list.
settings.pagination.paginate.hint:
Changes how long lists are shown across Gubbins — the **Inventory** list, the **Activity** feed and your **Contacts**.

- **Off** (the default) — one list that loads more as you scroll.
- **On** — the list is split into fixed-size **pages**, with a page control at the foot for stepping through them.

Either way, nothing about your data changes — only how the list is presented. Set the page size below.
settings.pagination.size.label: Items per page
settings.pagination.size.description: How many items each page shows when pagination is on ({min}–{max}).
settings.pagination.size.hint:
The number of items shown on each page when **Paginate long lists** is on. You can also change it from the page control at the foot of any paginated list — it’s the same shared setting.

Range {min}–{max}.
numberInput.srHint: This field accepts calculations — for example, type 500/2 and press Enter to work out the value.
numberInput.help:
**This box does maths.** Type a calculation and press **Enter** (or click away) to work out the value.

| You type | You get |
| --- | --- |
| `500/2` | `250` |
| `12*3` | `36` |
| `(2+3)*4` | `20` |
| `200*15%` | `30` |

Supports `+`, `−`, `×` (`*`), `÷` (`/`), `^` for powers, `%` (percent), and parentheses.
about.title: About
about.app.title: About Gubbins
about.app.intro.pre: Gubbins is a local-first, offline-capable app for tracking
about.app.intro.post: — electronics, 3D-printing supplies, tools, collections, and general inventory. Everything is stored privately on this device; nothing is sent to a server.
about.project.title: Project & support
about.project.body: The wiki has guides, tips and help. Source code, issue tracking and releases live on GitHub. Found a bug or have an idea? Please open an issue.
about.author.title: Author
about.privacy.title: Privacy
about.privacy.body: Local-first by design: all data is processed and stored entirely within your browser on this device. There is no account and no server-side data collection. Use the same browser profile to find your data again, and install the app or sync to a folder you control to keep a backup.
about.ai.title: AI-assisted development
about.ai.body: AI tooling was used in the development of this software.
about.licence.title: Licence & disclaimer
about.licence.disclaimer.pre: This software is provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind. You use it
about.licence.disclaimer.post: ; the developers accept no responsibility or liability for any loss, damage, data loss, or other issues arising from its use.
about.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
about.diagnostics.intro: Environment details that help when reporting a problem. Nothing is collected automatically or sent anywhere — details are gathered on this device only when you press Refresh, and never include your inventory.
about.diagnostics.empty: Press Refresh to gather diagnostics from this device.
about.diagnostics.privacyNote: The GitHub issue is public. Location-identifying details are redacted from it, and no inventory data is included.
boot.unsupported.detailsIntro: Worth including if you report this — it records exactly what Gubbins found on this device.
boot.unsupported.insecure.title: Gubbins needs a secure connection
boot.unsupported.insecure.lede: Your browser is almost certainly capable. This page just isn’t on a secure connection, so the browser is withholding the private storage Gubbins keeps your data in.
boot.unsupported.insecure.step2: Running it on this computer? Use an address starting “http://localhost” or “http://127.0.0.1” — browsers trust those. A network address such as “http://192.168.1.10” does not count as secure, so opening Gubbins from another device on your network needs https.
boot.unsupported.scripts.title: Something is blocking part of Gubbins
boot.unsupported.scripts.lede: This browser looks perfectly capable, but one of Gubbins’ own scripts never ran — which usually means something on this device is stopping it, rather than anything being wrong with the browser.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step1: Allow scripts for this site in your content or script blocker — then reload.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step2: To check whether an extension is responsible, open Gubbins in a window with extensions turned off.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step3: Antivirus software, a VPN, or a workplace or school network can filter pages too, and would affect every browser on this device.
boot.unsupported.siteData.title: Gubbins isn’t allowed to store anything here
boot.unsupported.siteData.lede: Your browser supports Gubbins, but site data is blocked for this site. Gubbins keeps your inventory on your own device, so without it there is nowhere to put your data.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step1: Allow cookies and site data for this site in your browser’s settings, then reload.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step2: “Block all cookies”, and the strictest tracking-protection modes, also switch off the storage Gubbins needs. An exception for this site is enough — no other site is affected.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step3: Private and incognito windows restrict storage as well. Try an ordinary window.
boot.unsupported.pending.title: Preparing secure storage…
boot.unsupported.pending.lede: Gubbins is setting up the private, offline storage it keeps your data in. This happens once, on your first visit, and the page carries on by itself as soon as it’s ready.
boot.unsupported.pending.note: Still here after a few moments? Reloading usually finishes the job.
boot.unsupported.isolation.title: Gubbins can’t finish setting up storage
boot.unsupported.isolation.lede: Your browser looks capable, but the background helper that unlocks Gubbins’ private storage couldn’t start. That points at this browser’s settings or an add-on rather than the browser itself.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step1: Private and incognito windows switch background helpers off. Try an ordinary window.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step2: A content blocker or privacy extension may be blocking it — allow this site, then reload.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step3: Antivirus software, a VPN, or a workplace or school network can alter pages in a way that prevents this.
boot.unsupported.browser.title: Browser not supported
boot.unsupported.browser.lede: Everything else on this device checks out, so this really does look like the browser: it’s missing the private, secure storage Gubbins needs to keep your data safe.
boot.unsupported.browser.step1: Try the latest Chrome, Edge, or Firefox.
boot.unsupported.browser.step2: On iPhone or iPad, add Gubbins to your Home Screen first, then open it from there.

dashboard.gettingStarted.body: Your inventory is empty. Add something by hand, bring in an existing list as a CSV, or scan a barcode to get started.
dashboard.backupNudge.heading: Keep your inventory safe
dashboard.backupNudge.body: Gubbins stores everything privately in this browser. Set up Cloud Sync or take a backup so a browser clear-out, a lost device, or a new browser can’t lose your inventory.
dashboard.wipBanner.heading: Work in progress
dashboard.wipBanner.body: Updates may not be backwards compatible, so data loss is expected. Backwards compatibility will be maintained once Gubbins reaches its 1.0 release.
dashboard.wipBanner.confirmBody.pre: Gubbins is still pre-release. Until version 1.0 is officially released, an update may not be backwards compatible and
dashboard.wipBanner.confirmNote: Hiding this warning does not remove that risk — please keep your own backups until 1.0 lands.

dashboard.nav.tooltip.inventory:
**Inventory** — your item catalogue.

Browse, search and filter every item, adjust stock by location, scan barcodes, and manage categories, locations, batches and cycle counts.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.projects:
**Projects** — build & job workspaces.

Track each project’s bill of materials, reserve and consume stock, manage a **budget** with an expense ledger, and follow its status.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.purchaseOrders:
**Purchase orders** — procurement.

Raise and receive POs against your suppliers, handle **partial / split receipts**, and watch in-transit stock land back in inventory.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.reports:
**Reports** — analytics & insight.

Stock valuation, **ABC analysis**, turnover & aging, spend over time, supplier costs and a data-hygiene checklist — all exportable to CSV.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.contacts:
**Contacts** — people & suppliers.

Your address book of suppliers and contacts, with their linked **supplier parts**, pricing and price history.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.bookings:
**Bookings** — reserve assets ahead.

Whole-day reservations of bookable items shown on a calendar, with overlap checks and one-click **convert to checkout**.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.upcoming:
**Upcoming** — your agenda.

Every date-driven event — due maintenance, expiring stock, bookings and PO deliveries — gathered into one timeline, **bucketed by when** it’s due.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.activity:
**Activity** — the global timeline.

A read-only feed of **every change across all items**, newest first, with filters by action type.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.alerts:
**Alerts** — what needs attention.

Low-stock, expiring, overdue and **budget** warnings gathered into one actionable list. The badge shows how many are active.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.sync:
**Sync** — cloud backup & devices.

Back up and restore your vault, and **sync changes between devices** so your inventory follows you.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.homeAssistant:
**Home Assistant** — voice control setup.

An interactive, step-by-step guide to ask **“where are my …?”** from Home Assistant — run the bridge, connect it, and generate an access token.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.settings:
**Settings** — preferences.

Theme, currency & locale, scanner options, low-stock thresholds, kiosk mode and the rest of the app’s behaviour.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.about:
**About** — app & storage info.

Version, storage usage, platform capabilities and project information.
